# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 14 (PNEUMA Dynamic)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 14
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Good. But I also want to show you this: what is the covenant, who is it for, and when was it given?
2. The commandments were given through Moses, but they were given for them. The covenant, however, was given for us. But notice how it was received: Moses received it as a servant. But the Lord himself gave the new covenant directly to us — so that we would be the people that truly knows him.
3. So our hope is in Jesus: through his own suffering he established the new covenant for us. The promise that had been made to the ancestors was sitting unclaimed — no one was worthy to receive it. He came to destroy death and to rescue that promise from the darkness.
4. He appeared to those very people who were hunting down and murdering his prophets — enduring everything on their account — revealed at the very end of the age, so that he could redeem from death those who had no other way to be redeemed.
5. He appeared to bring the full tally of sins committed against his prophets to its final completion.
6. He appeared, too, to call those whom God had prepared long in advance. When he came, he found us ready to receive him — not because we were righteous, but not because we were drowning in sin either. We had simply been prepared to receive the Lord.
7. And so, gathering the forgiveness of sins into himself, he gave us the name of the new people.
